style: Avant-garde garage rock and trashy music-hall brass band. Quartal suspended chord fields and microtonal micro-intervals rubbing against diatonic swagger. Fast chromatic cabaret patter opening into wide operatic melisma and hocketed spoken fragments. Deep funk-pocket groove invaded by irregular duple accents, asymmetric 7/8 stomps, and hard punk silences. Upright slap bass, distorted baritone sax, cheap pump organ, surf spring reverb, and dry close-miked drumkit. Theatrical overstatement, hyper-articulate nervous energy, and deadpan urgency. 1960s mono tape saturation with abrupt frequency gating, heavy spring splashes, and sudden room collapse. The band switches between marching-band bombast and sleazy nightclub swing while a frantic radio host screens callers from an alien dimension.
lyrics:
[SCENE START: ALIEN CALL-IN RADIO BROADCAST]
[TRANSMISSION CARRIER: 104.9 MEGA-HURTZ PLASMA BAND]
[HOST VOICE: OVER-CAFFEINEFIED WILDLIFE NARRATOR WITH TRASHY HYPE TONE]

[Intro: distorted baritone sax honks, dry slap bass thuds, rapid radio static burst]

[Host Spoken Monologue]
Attention listeners across all seventeen radial sectors! You are tuned directly into Frequency Sixty-Six: the only call-in show broadcasting from the wrong side of the page-wheel! I am your host, observing the local specimen behaviors in their natural neon habitat. And boy, are they leaking carrier waves today! Let us check the hold queue. Caller One, you are live through the subspace static. State your biological classification and why your furniture is currently screaming at the ceiling!

[Verse 1: Fast cabaret patter, tight garage-rock guitar stabs, irregular 7/8 meter]
[Caller One - Bleating Audio Feed]
My collarbone is folding backward into yesterday!
The floor tile smells like Tuesday morning's overdue tax form!
I tried to lock the front door, but the lock became a lizard!
It keeps blinking at my left retinal quadrant, mister host!
What do I do with the excessive velocity of my kitchen table?

[Chorus: Massed close-harmony doo-wop vocals with trashy theatrical overstatement]
[Full Ensemble Singalong]
Oh, the page is turning, the spine is cracking wide!
We are living in the margins where the logic went and died!
Keep your tentacles inside the vehicle and check your carrier wave!
There is no way out of the broadcast once you start to misbehave!
Yeah! Trash-tier reality! Keep the frequency hot!

[Post-Chorus: Hocketed spoken fragments, erratic drum fills, spring reverb crash]
[Host Interruption]
Put them on hold! Put them on the infinite loop behind the refrigerator! That is standard territorial etiquette in sector four, folks! Never let a bleeding specimen explain its own geometry while the transmission is this greasy!

[Verse 2: Swing rhythm invading punk-rock stomp, pump organ drone, nasally vocal lead]
[Host Calling Next Line]
Let us patch in Caller Two. You are leaking data packets across the dancefloor, friend. Speak into the microphone before the security squids arrive with the sanitizer buckets!

[Caller Two - Tremolo Voice and Static Whine]
I went down to the Alien Nightclub to watch the carbon units dance!
They were moving their mandibles completely out of phase with the baseline!
Every time the bass drum hit, my memories of childhood turned into soup!
I lost my passport inside a bowl of synthetic clam chowder!
Can anyone hear this signal? My skin is turning into radio static!

[Bridge: Slow-down metric compression, eerie barbershop vocal quartets, microtonal rubbing]
[Station ID Interlude]
You are listening to the sound of a civilisation forgetting how to spell its own name.
[Voice distortion increases, tape flutter speeds up]
Salvia page-wheel turning... Turn the page... Turn the page... Turn the spine...
Notice the color of the background noise. It is purple. It smells like copper.

[Guitar Solo: Frenetic, jagged garage-rock surf guitar with heavy spring reverb and microtonal bends]

[Verse 3: Fast scat-singing, marching-band snare cadence, hyper-articulate nervous energy]
[Host Scream]
We are back! The page-wheel just clicked another notch forward and my left ear is now a toaster! Let us take one more desperate call from the deep vacuum outside!

[Caller Three - Distorted High-Register Falsetto]
I am calling from inside a grandfather clock made entirely of liquid regret!
The pendulum keeps striking hours that have not been invented yet!
My shoes are arguing with my hat about who owns the copyright to my lungs!
Help me, radio host! The floor is tilting at forty-five degrees toward the toaster!

[Final Chorus: Massive operatic melisma crashing against garage-punk wall of sound]
[Full Ensemble Massed Voices]
Oh, the page is turning, the spine is cracking wide!
We are living in the margins where the logic went and died!
Keep your tentacles inside the vehicle and check your carrier wave!
There is no way out of the broadcast once you start to misbehave!

[Outro: Abrupt frequency cutoff, telephone dial tone fading into deep space vacuum hum]
[Host Final Word]
That is all our bandwidth for today, specimens. Remember to feed your household appliances and keep your carrier frequencies aligned with the local zoning laws. Goodnight from the wrong side of the wheel!
[Final Static Burst / Silence]
caption: A frantic alien call-in radio broadcast hosted by an erratic wildlife narrator inside a surreal nightclub. Driven by avant-garde garage rock, trashy brass, and cabaret patter, the song layers radio-wave signal decay, aberrant salience, and salvia page-wheel mechanics into a high-energy structural meltdown.
